Section 8B allows HMRC to withdraw a notice under section 8 or 8A within a defined withdrawal period, generally 2 years from the end of the relevant tax year, unless a return has already been made or a s.28C determination served. note.summary: This chunk sets out the requirement (TMA 1970 s.12AB) for a partnership return to include a partnership statement showing income/loss, disposal consideration, and tax deducted per source, plus each partner's share, including special rules for tiered partnerships (a partnership as partner in another partnership) and required assumptions about UK/non-UK residence and individual/company status of participating partnerships. Section 12ABZA removes the requirement to declare a partner's tax reference in certain overseas-investor scenarios where equivalent information is reported under the International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015, but requires notification to HMRC within 12 months of the filing date if that reliance later fails. Section 12ABZAA treats a purported partnership return for an LLP not actually carrying on business with a view to profit as a partnership return for purposes of enquiry and follower notice/accelerated payment provisions, extending partner/partnership terminology to LLP members and the purported partnership.

note.summary: Section 7 TMA 1970 requires a person chargeable to income tax or capital gains tax for a year of assessment, who has not received (or has had withdrawn) a notice to file under section 8, to notify HMRC of chargeability within a specified notification period. The notification period is 6 months from the end of the year of assessment, or, where a section 8 notice was withdrawn, the later of that 6-month period or 30 days from withdrawal. Subsection (3) exempts persons whose total income is entirely from sources already taxed at source or under PAYE, who have no chargeable gains, and who owe no additional tax under section 30 ITA 2007 (other than the winter fuel payment charge). Special provisions extend rules to trustees of settlements and define 'relevant trustees'. Persons notified of a simple assessment need not give notice unless additional tax/CGT is owed outside that assessment.

note.summary: Section 12AA sets out HMRC's power to require a partnership return, establishing each partner's chargeable income/corporation tax amounts, including for indirect partners in tiered partnerships. It prescribes filing deadlines that differ for electronic vs non-electronic returns and for partnerships including individuals versus companies, plus exceptions where notice is given late. It also requires declarations of partners' details and correctness, allows HMRC to demand additional information by regulation (subject to a £60 penalty for non-compliance), and defines terms like 'successor', 'relevant partner' and 'partnership return'. Section 12AAA (new) allows a partner to request withdrawal of a s.12AA notice within a specified withdrawal period, with conditions and interaction with penalty-cancellation provisions.

note.summary: Section 9 requires returns under section 8 or 8A to include a self-assessment of income tax and capital gains tax chargeable, and of the balance payable after deducting tax deducted at source, subject to exceptions for certain pension scheme and employer-financed retirement benefits scheme tax. Taxpayers are excused from self-assessing if they file by 31 October following the year of assessment, or within two months of a notice issued after 31 August. Section 9ZA allows a taxpayer to amend their personal or trustee return within twelve months of the filing date (31 January of Year 2, or three months from a late notice). Section 9ZB allows an HMRC officer to correct obvious errors, omissions, or other incorrect matters in a return within nine months of delivery (or of a taxpayer amendment), subject to the taxpayer's right to reject the correction within 30 days.

It sets statutory filing deadlines (31 October for non-electronic, 31 January for electronic returns) with exceptions for late-issued notices, requires a declaration of correctness, allows different requirements for different persons/periods, and imposes a £60 penalty for failing to provide additional information requested under new regulatory powers (subsection (1I)). Section 8ZA defines who counts as a person 'within section 8(4A)' for cross-border employment cases.

note.summary: Section 12AD governs the effect of a taxpayer amendment to a partnership return (or referral of a dispute to the tribunal) made while an enquiry into that return is in progress: the amendment does not restrict the enquiry's scope but is taken into account, and any effect on the partnership statement is deferred until a partial or final closure notice is issued, with specific rules on when the amendment does or does not take effect. note.summary: This chunk sets out rules for partnership returns under Self Assessment: a partnership return is conclusive as to partnership shares (s.12ABZB), subject to a tribunal referral process for disputes about shares (not profit amounts) within 12 months of delivery/amendment. It also covers taxpayer amendment of partnership returns (s.12ABA, within 12 months of filing date), Revenue correction of obvious errors or other incorrect matters (s.12ABB, within 9 months, subject to taxpayer rejection within 30 days), and HMRC's power to give notice of enquiry into partnership returns (s.12AC), including time limits, scope limitations following amendments/referrals, and deemed enquiry notices to individual partners.
